item.title: U.N. experts say U.S. may have committed war crimes with 2 Iran strikes
item.description: U.N.-commissioned rights experts say there are "reasonable grounds" to believe the U.S. committed war crimes with strikes that killed scores of Iranian civilians.

item.title: Conspiracy theories and the American presidency
item.description: In his new book "Conspirator in Chief," historian Stephen F. Knott argues that there is a long history of those who occupy the Oval Office engaging in conspiracy theories. Knott joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Iran recently downed at least 2 American drones, officials say
item.description: U.S. officials tell CBS News that Iran downed at least two American drones in recent days. CBS News' James Laporta reports.

item.title: GOP Rep. Maria Salazar says some of Trump's immigration enforcement efforts have "gone too far"
item.description: In a rare rebuke, Republican Rep. Maria Salazar of Florida criticized President Trump's immigration policy in a new campaign ad, saying some of his enforcement efforts have "gone too far." CBS News political director Fin Gómez and Republican strategist Sarah Chamberlain join with analysis.

item.title: Utah Gov. Spencer Cox on AI regulation: "If we're wrong, the consequences could be existential"
item.description: In a new book, Utah Republican Gov. Spencer Cox is urging Americans to tone down violent political rhetoric and, in his own words, "stop shooting at each other." Cox joins "The Takeout" to discuss the issue and recent concerns about artificial intelligence threatening humanity.

item.title: New bill aims to help wrongfully-detained Americans upon return to U.S.
item.description: Two years after Russia released Paul Whelan from a wrongful detention that lasted over five years, the Marine veteran is working with Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens of Michigan to try to make life easier for people like him upon their return to the U.S. Whelan and Stevens join "The Takeout" to unpack the proposed legislation.

item.title: Congressman breaks down bipartisan FRONTIER Act on AI oversight
item.description: Rep. Jay Obernolte, co-chair of the Congressional AI Caucus, joins CBS News to discuss AI industry leaders' existential warnings about the threat the technology poses to humans. He also discusses the FRONTIER Act he introduced to strengthen oversight on AI.

item.title: U.N. panel says "reasonable grounds" to believe U.S. committed war crimes with two strikes in Iran
item.description: A U.N. human rights panel says they have found "reasonable grounds" that the U.S. committed war crimes during two airstrikes in Iran, including one at a school. Marine Corps veteran and former CIA officer Elliot Ackerman joins with analysis.

item.title: Aly Raisman shares 3 things people can do to advocate for themselves
item.description: Olympic gold medalist Aly Raisman shared the three things people can do to advocate for themselves.

item.title: Why the Trump administration is so focused on vaccines
item.description: Robert F. Kennedy Jr. delivered a keynote speech Thursday at a conference for Children's Health Defense, an anti-vaccine group. CBS News medical correspondent Dr. Céline Gounder discusses why the Trump administration has focused so much on vaccines.

item.title: Farmer who voted for Trump says farmers are "all just in survival mode"
item.description: Matt Bell said he initially supported Trump's policies but now feels he and other farmers were "sold a bill of goods" that there was a plan to "put America's farmers and ranchers first."

item.title: Trump photo shows him viewing "Kennedy Center demolished" document
item.description: In court documents filed Wednesday by Rep. Joyce Beatty, a witness said he saw a "forklift run into and hit the pillars" of the building.

item.title: Rep. Ted Lieu pushes for AI regulation: "Humans must be in control of AI, not the other way around"
item.description: With greater frequency these last few months, artificial intelligence models are acting in unexpected and alarming ways. Democratic Rep. Ted Lieu of California joins "The Takeout" to discuss what congressional regulation could look like.

item.title: Anthropic says terror groups used AI for weapons development, planning
item.description: Anthropic says terror groups in the Middle East and Africa have tried to use the Claude AI chatbot to develop weapons and attack plans. CBS News' Leigh Kiniry reports, and Rep. Jay Obernolte, co-chair on the Congressional AI Caucus, discusses how he plans to strengthen oversight.

item.title: Kennedy Center official says "nothing is being demolished" as Trump says it could be "ripped down"
item.description: A spokesperson for the Kennedy Center says "nothing is being demolished" after President Trump said it could be "ripped down" unless the building bore his name. CBS News digital politics reporter Kathryn Watson has the details.

item.title: Aly Raisman details ordeal to schedule an appointment with a specialist for her period pain
item.description: Aly Raisman told Norah O'Donnell on "Healthful" her struggle to schedule an appointment with a specialist to address her painful periods. She said she's seen three doctors, who have all cleared her to see a specialist, but she's now on a yearlong waiting list to schedule an appointment.

item.title: Philadelphia "house of horrors" at center of investigation into possible serial murders
item.description: Philadelphia police, along with the FBI, are investigating possible serial murders in the city. This comes after investigators discovered evidence tied to at least five missing women in a home in the city's Olney neighborhood. CBS Philadelphia reporter Joe Holden has the latest.

item.title: F-16 from Texas crashes in Michigan, evacuation order issued
item.description: Blair Township Supervisor Nicole Blonshine said she was told the aircraft was an F-16 but does not have "100% confirmation." The pilot parachuted out before it crashed, she said.

item.title: Iran downed at least 2 American drones in recent days, U.S. officials say
item.description: Iranian forces in recent days have brought down at least two American MQ-1 unmanned aircraft, according to U.S. officials familiar with the matter.

item.title: Iran downed at least 2 unmanned American aircraft in recent days, U.S. officials say
item.description: CBS News has learned that Iranian forces took down at least two American MQ-1 unmanned aircraft in recent days, according to U.S. officials familiar with the incident. CBS News' James LaPorta has more.

item.title: From the archives: Bob Mackie on being dressmaker to the stars
item.description: Nine-time Emmy-winning costume designer Bob Mackie, who clothed such musical and comedic talents as Cher, Carol Burnett, Barbra Streisand and Liza Minnelli, died on Sept. 14, 2026 at age 87. In this Sept. 21, 2003 "Sunday Morning" profile, Mackie talked with correspondent Rita Braver about how a star-struck kid growing up outside Hollywood became a dressmaker to the stars, and what fascinates him about divas. He also talked about the tragic death of his son, Robin, from AIDS.

item.title: White House withdraws ICE director nominee Richard Schroyer
item.description: Richard Schroyer's nomination was held up in the Senate. The White House eventually pulled it.

item.title: "48 Hours" show schedule
item.description: "48 Hours" uncovers the narrative behind true crime cases with unmatched reporting and suspense.

item.title: No relief in sight for U.S. drivers as gas and diesel prices surge
item.description: The Iran war and Russia-Ukraine conflict are knocking out global refining capacity, pushing fuel prices higher, analysts said.

item.title: 3 savings moves to make post-Fed rate hike
item.description: The Federal Reserve raised interest rates this week. Here are three savvy moves savers should make in response.

item.title: 1 in 3 Americans with health insurance have medical debt, survey finds
item.description: Nearly half of Americans with medical debt owe at least $2,000, forcing them to make tough choices, new research shows.

item.title: Grand Teton park forced to kill bear due to visitors' "poor decisions"
item.description: A black bear was euthanized in Grand Teton National Park after "poor decisions" made by human visitors, according to park officials.

item.title: Ross Fire 100% contained after more than 3 weeks
item.description: The wildfire, which has torn through Palo Pinto and Jack counties, forced evacuations, closed roads and disrupted schools.

item.title: There are more trucks on U.S. highways. But the government is inspecting them less.
item.description: A CBS News investigation finds that more than 600 people have died in crashes since 2024 with trucks operated by companies that had never been subjected to a roadside safety inspection.

item.title: Border Patrol officer indicted for sexually assaulting, robbing 4 women
item.description: A Chicago Border Patrol agent is facing federal charges for allegedly sexually assaulting four women at Chicago area hotels while on the job in 2022.
